"V" Is for Vagina
is the debut studio album by
Maynard James Keenan
's
side project
Puscifer
, released on October 30, 2007. The album features a significantly different,
electronic
sound and
arrangements
than Keenan's other bands: the
progressive
Tool
and
alternative
A Perfect Circle
. Keenan himself compared the sound of
"V" Is for Vagina
to "driving around in your car listening to those old
Motown
hits,
James Brown
, and cool
R&B
stuff".
[
4
]
"V" is for Vagina
has sold 112,000 copies.
[
5
]
Release
The album was preceded by a non-album, retail-only single called "
Cuntry Boner
", released on October 2, 2007. Released a week later was an
iTunes
-only four track
EP
titled
Don't Shoot the Messenger
, with tracks previously released only on soundtracks.
On October 30, 2007, a second single, and first actual radio single from the album, "
Queen B.
" was posted into a flash audio player on the official website, along with selected tracks by Keenan projects. On October 1, 2007, the video was posted on the Puscifer
YouTube
channel.
[
6
]
The video features several fully CGI Maynards as pawns in a chess game between two women. The album debuted at number 25 on the
Billboard
200
, selling about 27,000 copies in its first week.
[
7
]
On October 7, 2007, "Trekka (Sean Beaven Mix)" was published on Puscifer.com, and on October 25, 2007, the entire album was put up for listening.
On October 17, 2008, an official music video for the song "Momma Sed" was released online via the official Puscifer
YouTube
channel.
[
8
]
The vinyl edition of
"V" is for Vagina
was re-released in August 2016.
Remix albums
On April 28, 2008, a
remix album
with versions of tracks from
"V" Is for Vagina
was released, entitled
"V" Is for Viagra. The Remixes
.
[
9
]
In 2022 another remix titled
"V" is for Versatile
released.
